basis: Fixes the four non-blocking documentation-accuracy findings of the CTO review of cc85bcc on AFC-260 (verdict APPROVED). All four are the same class: the guard's prose about its own limits overstated what its code did, in the one section whose stated purpose is to prevent unstated limits. N1 (one line, documentation only): the header's COMPLETE LIST of audited shapes omitted Makefile, and the word Makefile appeared nowhere in the file, while the reviewer measured the coverage as CORRECT in both directions -- a tab-indented recipe is command position to the matcher, which only requires that a line NAMES this script. The list now names Makefile, and 11h now plants both recipe shapes in both directions so the claim is earned by a test rather than asserted in prose. N2 (behavioural, chosen over option (a)): the header and the AFC-256 claim both asserted 'a token sitting immediately before a metacharacter is a redirection, never an argument'. That is true for an UNQUOTED token and false for one that ENDED IN A CLOSING QUOTE, which is a complete argument: `--check-commit "$PWD" "$range">out.txt` is two arguments and was NOT flagged, a false negative on the exact shape the assertion exists to catch, opposite in direction to the finding AFC-241 blocked on. Rather than scope the sentence down to the weaker claim, the counter now carries a qtok flag and the discard is conditional on the pending token not having closed a quote, so the sentence becomes TRUE as originally written. Both directions are planted in 11h (four new shapes: "$range">out.txt, "$range"&, and their two-argument counterparts). The AFC-256 claim file repeated the overclaim verbatim and is corrected in place with this issue named, because a claim file is read by people who never open the script. N3 (one line): the refusal printed `$#`, which counts the flag, so it said it ignored 4 arguments and listed 3; it now prints `$(( $# - 1 ))`, and 11i asserts the said count equals the number of names printed rather than trusting either. N4 (behavioural): the header claimed 'the DISPATCHER refuses a surplus argument on its own', which held for --check-commit only -- `guard "" ROOT SURPLUS` returned byte-identical output to `guard "" ROOT`, exit 0 both times, the same defect class in the sibling branch. The fix went into the dispatcher, not into the sentence, because a paragraph that must be weakened every time the code turns out to be right is a paragraph that gets believed over the code; root mode now refuses a surplus with exit 2, naming what it ignored, and 11i drives both modes. VERIFIED at this commit: --self-test 36 assertions; the eleven shapes pinned by the AFC-260 verdict all behave as that verdict recorded (6 one-argument unflagged, 5 two-argument caught) plus the four N2 shapes in both directions; exit codes re-measured at THIS build rather than carried forward from cc85bcc, per N5 -- 84e65f7 exit 1, 65e7631 exit 1, HEAD exit 1, not-a-revision exit 2; GUARDED_PATHS and REVIEW_REQUIRED_PATHS byte-identical to 7b61b30. MUTANTS, each by exact literal replacement in a throwaway clone, each caught by a named assertion: tab-indented recipes stop matching (11h, 'flagged 8 of 9'); discard made unconditional (11h, 'flagged 7 of 9'); refusal counts $# (11i, 'says it ignored 3 and lists 2'); root-mode refusal removed (11i, 'root mode refused without naming it'); and the two AFC-241 mutants re-checked because the binding must not have rotted -- constant raised to 2 (11e, 11f, 11h, 11i red) and dispatcher widened (11e, 11i red). Assertion count is unchanged at 36: AFC-269 landed between cc85bcc and this commit and added four, so the AFC-278 constraint's 'must stay at 32' was already stale; the two assertions that gained coverage (11h, 11i) were extended in place rather than adding a 37th. NOT FIXED HERE, AND DELIBERATELY SO: while verifying, --self-test was found RED on a clean clone of main, cause merge-in-gate.sh:125 -- a wrapped English sentence in another agent's committed documentation block that begins in command position with the script path and the flag, so the matcher reads 'that the CI file' as four arguments. That is a fifth instance of the same cries-wolf class, in a file this commit does not own and cannot attribute to a live agent's unreviewed work, and the two available fixes are both decisions that are not mine: reword another author's compliance-path documentation, or loosen a compliance matcher so a gate goes green. Neither is taken silently. Raised as a blocking child issue with the measurement. No change to scripts/retention-literal-gate.sh or scripts/run-db-tests.mjs, no migration, no engine change, no privilege change, no personal data, so the CTO migration-approval path is not engaged. This claim carries no Reviewed-by trailer: the commit is UNREVIEWED and is raised to MediaTech (CTO). There is no independent security reviewer on this team -- the board declined that seat on cost -- so a CTO self-review is a recorded degradation, not independent review.

afc283Review.whyNotARecordedR2Review: A reviews[] entry would assert that R2's requirement -- a named reviewer who is not the author -- is met. It is not met in the sense that matters: this commit is git-attributed to cto@afc.local (verified: shared-repo git config user.email = cto@afc.local, user.name = AFC CTO (MediaTech)), and the only reviewer available on this team is the CTO. Per AFC-194 section 5 and the CEO ruling of 2026-10-06, a CTO review of a CTO-team compliance commit is a disclosure, not a second signature, and must not be entered as R2 satisfaction. This follows the cc85bcc precedent: after the AFC-260 review of cc85bcc, AFC-256.json carries no reviews[] entry and the debt is declared. scripts/dirty-path-guard.sh is not on REVIEW_REQUIRED_PATHS, so R2 does not machine-apply to 28430fb; this declaration suppresses no violation and clears no red. The R2 debt stands.
afc283Review.findings: F1 (low, non-blocking): the claim and the AFC-283 request cite md5 7baef0ee / 42bf4be1 for GUARDED_PATHS / REVIEW_REQUIRED_PATHS. Neither reproduces under any standard extraction; the substantive invariant -- the two arrays are byte-identical between 28430fb and 7b61b30 -- is independently TRUE. Drop the digest or record the exact command. F2 (provenance, recorded not fixed): the git author is cto@afc.local while this file's authorAgentId is the Coder (7b4aae3b-0da5-4de2-a1d8-4737943ef561). Decision: the registry's authorAgentId is the authoritative authorship source for R1; the git author is not authoritative and must not be used to judge review independence. F3 (process, pre-existing): no independent reviewer seat exists; a CTO review is a recorded degradation, not independent review.
afc283Review.verified: Independent, in a clean clone. --self-test at 28430fb and 28430fb~1: identical failure set, exit 1 both, single FAIL = merge-in-gate.sh:125 (pre-existing, introduced in 2ef97d8, untouched by this commit); 35 ok + 1 FAIL = 36; output diff is exactly the three changed assertion lines. N2 matcher driven directly: two-arg "$PWD" "$range">out.txt unflagged at parent, flagged at HEAD; one-arg "$range">out.txt unflagged at both; 17-shape battery HEAD 9 flagged vs parent 7, HEAD a strict superset, additions exactly the two N2 two-arg shapes; qtok can only increment the count. N3 via CLI: HEAD 'Refusing 2' lists 2; parent 'Refusing 3' lists 2. N4 via CLI: HEAD exit 2 naming ignored-a/ignored-b; parent exit 0 silent. GUARDED_PATHS and REVIEW_REQUIRED_PATHS byte-identical to 7b61b30. Issue: AFC-278 trailer present and parsed.
